text:
ana: Heads up — docusaurus build failing on the onboarding guide. linkcheck shows broken fragment for '#getting-started- ' (looks like a trailing dash/space mess).

sam: hmm, saw that last week. MDX and docusaurus slugify differ on punctuation. A heading ending with a hyphen can produce an extra dash in slug or leave a trailing space in some locales.

ana: here's the error from linkbot: `Broken links found: /docs/onboarding#getting-started- `

linkbot: detected 3 affected files: docs/onboarding.md, docs/onboarding.es.md, docs/onboarding.zh-CN.md. Suggested fix: normalize headings and add explicit ids.

devex-lee: quick pragmatic approach — add explicit ids for those headings: `## Getting started {#getting-started}`. That prevents the auto-slugger from guessing differently across builds.

sam: agree. Also we should run a script to find headings that end with punctuation or whitespace. I have one-liner: `rg "^#{1,6} .*[[:punct:] ]$" docs/ --line-number` — lists suspicious headings.

ana: i pushed a tiny cleanup patch that removes trailing punctuation and adds explicit ids where the heading had to keep punctuation for correctness. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2120

devex-lee: can we enforce in CI? I'd rather not silently remove punctuation from headings. Instead, add a pre-publish linter that flags headings with trailing whitespace or punctuation that could change slugs, and fail the build with a helpful message.

ci-bot: new job docs/anchor-lint started. It runs `node scripts/anchor-lint.js` and checks built site fragments.

sam: small gotcha — some localized translations intentionally have punctuation differences that change slugs. The sync script needs to map explicit IDs from the source. docs-bot: when upstream heading has `{#id}` the localized files should preserve `<!-- original-id: getting-started -->` or include the same `{#getting-started}`.

linkbot: added note: run `yarn docs:sync` after making header id edits to propagate to locales. If a locale needs a different translation that changes meaning, mark it with a localized explicit id: `{#getting-started-zh}` and update crosslinks accordingly.

ana: test plan in PR: 1) run anchor-lint to fail on trailing whitespace/punct; 2) run built site fragment resolution and ensure no 404s; 3) include a small README snippet for translators about preserving header ids.

sam: nit on implementation: prefer HTML comment style fallback for MDX-only flows `<!-- id:getting-started -->` because some render pipelines strip attribute-style ids. But either approach is fine as long as the id is stable.

devex-lee: i'll add both examples to docs/style.md and include a tiny unit test for anchor-lint that feeds a small mdx sample and asserts the extracted id equals `getting-started`.

ci-bot: build #5874 queued for PR 2120 — includes anchor-lint and locale-sync reminder.

linkbot: FYI — i found 12 headings across the repo that match the risk regex. Logged them in the PR for manual review.

ana: thanks everyone. merging after CI green. Will follow up with a short Slack post in #docs summarizing the new rule so folks updating docs know how to handle translated headings.

ci-bot: build #5874 passed. linkcheck and anchor-lint green :white_check_mark:
